hook.say: This morning I covered United banning outside AI agents from booking flights, while Southwest opened its inventory to ChatGPT. I went back in to check the numbers.

findings.label: INTERMEDIARY
findings.headline: Propellic reportedly puts agent bookings via a booking API at 57%
findings.detail: We could not find this figure on the cited page at check time.
findings.evidence: 57% of flight bookings would go through an intermediary
findings.say: First, Propellic is said to have found 57% of agent flight bookings go through an intermediary, but we could not confirm that on the page cited.

findings.label: DIRECT VISITS
findings.headline: AI models sent users straight to airline sites
findings.detail: Bain test of three LLMs on schedule and price searches. Online travel agencies dominated the results.
findings.evidence: airline websites were accessed directly only about 5% of the time
findings.say: Second, Bain tested three AI models on flight searches. They went directly to an airline website only about 5% of the time.

findings.label: SEARCH LOAD
findings.headline: possible searches per booking from AI queries
findings.detail: PhocusWire analysis. United already fines agencies that generate more search traffic than bookings.
findings.evidence: look-to-book ratios for AI-generated queries could exceed 200,000:1
findings.say: Third, PhocusWire's analysis says AI queries could reach 200,000 searches for every booking, which shows why airlines worry about cost.

take.headline: Draw the line, then measure who crosses it.
take.say: Drawing a line is a start, but who is really booking? If you use these agents, what do you see? Comment CHECK and tell me.

sources.title: Travel Daily News: Propellic study finds most agentic AI travel bookings go through intermediaries
Bain & Company: Is the Airline Industry Ready for Agent-Led Bookings?
Travelers Today: AI Travel Search Is Breaking Airline Systems

caption:
This morning: United banned outside AI agents from booking flights, while Southwest opened its inventory to ChatGPT. Two airlines, two opposite policies.

The data: Propellic is reported to say 57% of agent flight bookings go through an intermediary (NOT CONFIRMED: we could not find this figure on the cited Travel Daily News page). AI models went straight to airline sites only about 5% of the time (Bain). AI queries could hit 200,000 searches per booking (PhocusWire).

My take: drawing a line is the right start, but measure who is actually booking before you write the rule.

Comment CHECK and I will DM you what I find.

Sources in the first comment.
